Issues.Title: `canonicalize`: `console.log` of a plugin lands in stdout, before the results
Issues.Body:
**What version of Tailwind CSS are you using?**

v4.3.3, with `@tailwindcss/cli` and with the standalone CLI. On `main` (de2255b), `packages/@tailwindcss-cli/src/commands/canonicalize/index.ts` still loads the design system in the process that writes the results to `process.stdout`.

**What build tool (or framework if it abstracts the build tool) are you using?**

None. `tailwindcss canonicalize` of `@tailwindcss/cli` 4.3.3.

**What version of Node.js are you using?**

v26.10.0

**What browser are you using?**

N/A

**What operating system are you using?**

Linux

**Reproduction URL**

https://gist.github.com/rubas/92e64c757e6e51d98cc7cd7e9f60ec75

**Describe your issue**

`tailwindcss canonicalize` writes its results to stdout. When a plugin of the CSS entry calls `console.log` while it loads, that text lands in the same stream, before the results. A tool that reads the results gets one line too many, and the JSON output is no longer valid JSON.

`plugin.mjs`:

```js
export default function () {
  console.log("hello from a plugin")
}
```

`app.css`:

```css
@import "tailwindcss";
@plugin "./plugin.mjs";
```

```
$ npx tailwindcss canonicalize --css app.css "p-4 px-2 py-2"
hello from a plugin
p-2

$ npx tailwindcss canonicalize --css app.css --format json "p-4 px-2 py-2"
hello from a plugin
[
  {
    "input": "p-4 px-2 py-2",
    "output": "p-2",
    "changed": true
  }
]

$ printf 'p-4 px-2 py-2\nw-4 h-4\n' | npx tailwindcss canonicalize --css app.css --stream
hello from a plugin
p-2
size-4
```

I expect only the results on stdout, and the output of a plugin on stderr.

A real case: daisyUI prints a banner when it loads, unless its option `logs` is `false`. A formatter that reads one line per class list from `--stream` takes the banner as the first answer, and then writes each class list into the wrong element.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "`canonicalize`: `console.log` of a plugin lands in stdout, before the results" (#20560)

Issues.Title: Write plugin logs to stderr in `canonicalize`
Issues.Body:
## Summary

`tailwindcss canonicalize` writes its results to stdout, but the design system is loaded in the same process, so anything a plugin logs with `console.log` while it loads (e.g. the daisyUI banner) ends up in front of the results. That breaks `--format json` and shifts every line in `--stream` mode.

This points `console.log`, `console.info` and `console.debug` at `console.error` for the `canonicalize` command, so stdout only carries the results and plugin output goes to stderr.

Fixes #20560

## Test plan

Added an integration test with a plugin that calls `console.log`, it fails on `main` and passes with this change.

Also checked by hand with the reproduction from the issue:

```
$ tailwindcss canonicalize --css app.css "p-4 px-2 py-2" 2>/dev/null
p-2
$ printf 'p-4 px-2 py-2\nw-4 h-4\n' | tailwindcss canonicalize --css app.css --stream 2>/dev/null
p-2
size-4
```
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Write plugin logs to stderr in `canonicalize`" (#20561)

Issues.Title: @property fallback detection matches current Safari Technology Preview: margin-trim: inline is no longer valid CSS
Issues.Body:
**What version of Tailwind CSS are you using?**

v4 (seen in v4.1.0 output, still on main)

**What build tool (or framework if it abstracts the build tool) are you using?**

N/A, the issue is in the emitted CSS

**What version of Node.js are you using?**

N/A

**What browser are you using?**

Safari Technology Preview 254 (WebKit trunk since 2026-08-21)

**What operating system are you using?**

macOS

**Reproduction URL**

[minimal-testcase](https://bug-327332-attachments.webkit.org/attachment.cgi?id=481771)

This is affecting chatgpt.com and probably plenty of other sites.

**Describe your issue**

The `@property` fallback block is wrapped in

```
@supports ((-webkit-hyphens: none) and (not (margin-trim: inline))) or ((-moz-orient: inline) and (not (color:rgb(from red r g b))))
```

https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/blob/main/packages/tailwindcss/src/ast.ts

The Safari branch assumes `margin-trim: inline` is valid in every Safari that supports `@property`. **That is no longer true**. 

The CSS WG removed the inline values from margin-trim (https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/13731), the [grammar is now](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box-4/#margin-trim) `none | block | [ block-start || block-end ]`, and all three engines follow it:

- WebKit: https://commits.webkit.org/319622@main (Safari Technology Preview, future Safari releases)
- Chromium: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8256869, `margin-trim` shipped to stable afterwards
- Firefox: block values only, behind a pref

So `CSS.supports('margin-trim', 'inline')` is now `false` in Safari Technology Preview, and the fallback block applies in a browser that supports `@property`. Chrome and Firefox are not affected, since Chrome does not support `-webkit-hyphens` and Firefox supports `rgb(from ...)`.

When the properties layer comes first, the fallback is harmless. When it ends up after the utilities layer, the `* { --tw-*: ... }` resets win over the utilities. This happens on chatgpt.com today, where every `-translate-y-1/2` is lost in Safari Technology Preview and controls are drawn half their height too low.

Expected: the fallback does not apply in browsers that support `@property`.

A detection that does not depend on margin-trim's inline values would fix it. Already deployed CSS will keep the old condition, so we are also discussing a [compatibility workaround on the WebKit side](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=327332).
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "@property fallback detection matches current Safari Technology Preview: margin-trim: inline is no longer valid CSS" (#20568)

Issues.Title: Use `margin-trim: block` in the `@property` fallback detection
Issues.Body:
Fixes #20568.

## Summary

The `@property` fallback is gated on `not (margin-trim: inline)`. The CSSWG removed the inline values (w3c/csswg-drafts#13731), and Safari Technology Preview now rejects them, so the fallback resets override utilities there.

This switches to `margin-trim: block`. That value is still in the grammar and shipped with `@property` in [Safari 16.4](https://webkit.org/blog/13966/webkit-features-in-safari-16-4/), so the branch still matches only older Safari. Firefox's branch is unchanged.

I did not use `at-rule(@property)`: browsers without `at-rule()` support would evaluate `not at-rule(…)` as true.

## Test plan

- `pnpm vitest run packages/tailwindcss/src/index.test.ts -t 'fallback detection'`: fails on `main`, passes here.
- `pnpm vitest run packages/tailwindcss`: 5107 passed, 1 skipped; snapshots updated for the new string.
- Not run locally: the `@tailwindcss/postcss` tests and the integration tests (no oxide native build here).

Prepared with AI assistance (Claude), reviewed and tested before submission.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Use `margin-trim: block` in the `@property` fallback detection" (#20569)

Issues.Title: Fix canonicalization of `theme(…)` alpha with more than 2 decimals
Issues.Body:
## Summary

This PR fixes two problems with how an inline `theme(…)` alpha is canonicalized to a candidate modifier.

### Alphas with more than 2 decimals

When canonicalizing an arbitrary property that uses an inline `theme(…)` with a fractional alpha that has more than 2 decimals, the opacity changed by a factor of 100.

For example, `[color:theme(colors.red.500/.12345)]` became `text-red-500/1234.5`. An arbitrary modifier without a unit is treated as a number and multiplied by 100, so the result had an opacity of `1234.5%` instead of `12.345%`.

This PR uses an arbitrary percentage instead, so `[color:theme(colors.red.500/.12345)]` now becomes `text-red-500/[12.345%]`.

While working on this, I also noticed floating point noise: `.29 * 100` is `28.999999999999996`, which would also have produced an arbitrary modifier. The value is now rounded first, so `[color:theme(colors.red.500/.29)]` becomes `text-red-500/29`.

### Custom `--opacity-*` theme values

A named modifier like `/50` reads from the `--opacity-*` theme values first. So if a theme already defines `--opacity-50: 10%`, then `[color:theme(colors.red.500/50%)]` became `text-red-500/50`, which is a 10% opacity instead of 50%. The same happened for `.12` → `/12` and `.29` → `/29`.

Now the named modifier is only used when there is no `--opacity-*` theme value for it, or when that value results in the same opacity (e.g. `--opacity-75: 0.75` or `--opacity-75: 75%`). Otherwise, an arbitrary percentage is used:

| Theme | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| no `--opacity-50` | `[color:theme(colors.red.500/50%)]` | `text-red-500/50` |
| `--opacity-50: 10%` | `[color:theme(colors.red.500/50%)]` | `text-red-500/[50%]` |
| `--opacity-75: 0.75` | `[color:theme(colors.red.500/75%)]` | `text-red-500/75` |

## Test plan

- Updated the existing `.12345` case and added a `.29` case in `canonicalize-candidates.test.ts`.
- Added cases with conflicting, matching and missing `--opacity-*` theme values, for both `@theme` and `@theme inline`. The conflicting cases fail on `main`.

```
pnpm vitest run packages/tailwindcss/src/canonicalize-candidates.test.ts
```
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Fix canonicalization of `theme(…)` alpha with more than 2 decimals" (#20563)

Issues.Title: Fix the intersection polyfill in canonicalizeCandidates
Issues.Body:
## Summary

The `intersection` helper in `canonicalize-candidates.ts` falls back to a polyfill when `Set.prototype.intersection` is missing (Node.js < 22). The polyfill copied the first set and never removed any item, so it returned the first set instead of the intersection. The collapse step gave different results on those Node.js versions.

The polyfill now keeps only the items of the first set that are also in the second set. The function is exported so the polyfill path can be tested directly.

## Test plan

Added unit tests for the polyfill path (the native method is stubbed out).

```
cd packages/tailwindcss
pnpm vitest run src/canonicalize-candidates.test.ts
```
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Fix the intersection polyfill in canonicalizeCandidates" (#20562)

Issues.Title: Fix the Nuxt dev mode integration test
Issues.Body:
## Summary

The `vite/nuxt.test.ts > dev mode` integration test fails on `main` on Linux, macOS and Windows since Vite 6.4.4 (released on 2026-10-06). The SSR render of `/` crashes, so the page has no styles:

```
[GET] "http://[::1]:3000/__nuxt_vite_node__/module//node_modules/.pnpm/ofetch@1.5.1/node_modules/ofetch/dist/node.mjs": 403 Forbidden
```

Nuxt 3.16.0 serves vite-node modules over HTTP. For each module id, it calls Vite's `isFileServingAllowed(config, id)`. These ids are root-relative URLs, like `/node_modules/.pnpm/...`. Before Vite 6.4.4, the import analysis plugin added these URLs to `safeModulePaths`, so the check passed. Vite 6.4.4 adds the resolved file paths instead (https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/23656), so the check now rejects the root-relative ids.

All Nuxt versions before 3.18.0 do this check. Nuxt 3.18.0 and later serve vite-node modules over an IPC socket without it. This PR moves the test to Nuxt 3.21.11, the latest 3.x release. It runs on Vite 7.3.7, which has the same `safeModulePaths` change.

It also removes the `nitropack: 2.11.0` pin. Nuxt 3.21 gets Nitro through `@nuxt/nitro-server` (`nitropack@^2.13.4`), so nothing used the pinned copy.

## Test plan

Locally on macOS, with `pnpm vitest --root=./integrations run vite/nuxt.test.ts`:

- Nuxt 3.16.0 and Vite 6.4.4: `dev mode` fails with the same 403 as CI.
- Nuxt 3.16.0 with a `vite: 6.4.3` override: both tests pass. This confirms the cause.
- Nuxt 3.21.11: both tests pass in 3 of 3 runs, with and without the `nitropack` pin.

CI checks Linux and Windows.

[ci-all]
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Fix the Nuxt dev mode integration test" (#20564)

Issues.Title: Canonicalization rewrites `[&_::pseudo-element]:*` to `**:[::pseudo-element]:*`, which is a syntax error
Issues.Body:
**What version of Tailwind CSS are you using?**

v4.3.3 (also reproduces on `0.0.0-insiders.fa81d69`)

**What build tool (or framework if it abstracts the build tool) are you using?**

@tailwindcss/cli 4.3.3 (`tailwindcss canonicalize`)

**What version of Node.js are you using?**

v26.10.0

**What browser are you using?**

Chrome

**What operating system are you using?**

macOS

**Reproduction URL**

https://play.tailwindcss.com/9dPXQ2weIo

**Describe your issue**

```sh
npx @tailwindcss/cli@4.3.3 canonicalize '[&_::before]:text-red-500'
# **:[::before]:text-red-500
```

The two classes are not equivalent:

```css
/* [&_::before]:text-red-500 */
.\[\&_\:\:before\]\:text-red-500 ::before { … }

/* **:[::before]:text-red-500 */
:is(.\*\*\:\[\:\:before\]\:text-red-500 *):is(::before) { … }
```

`[::before]` has no `&`, so it compiles to `&:is(::before)`. Pseudo-elements aren't valid inside `:is()`, so it's a syntax error. In the Play link, the first dot is red and the second (the canonical form) stays black.

The same thing happens for every pseudo-element without an equivalent named variant, e.g. `::before`, `::marker`, `::-webkit-scrollbar` and `::-webkit-search-cancel-button`. It also happens with the child combinator: `[&>::before]` → `*:[::before]`, which compiles to `:is(.… > *):is(::before)`. Other cases come out right:

- Pseudo-classes are fine: `[&_:hover]` → `**:[:hover]` compiles to `:is(.… *):is(:hover)`, which is equivalent.
- With a named variant it's fine: `[&_::placeholder]` → `**:placeholder`.

**Expected:** keep the `&`, i.e. `**:[&::before]:text-red-500`, which compiles to `:is(.… *)::before`, or leave the class unchanged. (`**:[&::before]:text-red-500` is already treated as canonical.)

**Cause:** This was introduced in a41add9f (#19178, first released in v4.1.16). That commit widened the `[&_X]` / `[&>X]` rewrites from attribute selectors to any `X` starting with `:`. It also added a fallback that emits `**:[X]` / `*:[X]` when `X` has no named variant. That's correct for pseudo-classes, which are the only cases its tests cover (`:first-child`, `:--custom`). But `::before` also starts with `:`, and the fallback drops the `&` that a pseudo-element needs.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Canonicalization rewrites `[&_::pseudo-element]:*` to `**:[::pseudo-element]:*`, which is a syntax error" (#20549)

Issues.Title: Canonicalization: keep `&` when moving a pseudo-element into `*` or `**`
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Fixes #20549.

`[&_::before]:flex` was canonicalized to `**:[::before]:flex`. An arbitrary variant without `&` compiles to `&:is(…)`, and pseudo-elements can't go inside `:is()`, so the canonical class generated an invalid selector.

When the `*`/`**` fallback moves a pseudo-element (anything starting with `::`, plus the legacy `:before`, `:after`, `:first-line` and `:first-letter`) into its own arbitrary variant, it now keeps the `&`, so `[&_::before]:flex` becomes `**:[&::before]:flex` and `[&>::before]:flex` becomes `*:[&::before]:flex`. Pseudo-classes still canonicalize to `**:[:hover]` as before.

## Test plan

Added `[&_::before]:flex`, `[&_>_::before]:flex`, `[&_:before]:flex` and `[&_>_:before]:flex` cases next to the existing `:--custom` ones in `canonicalize-candidates.test.ts`. They fail on `main` (`**:[::before]:flex`) and pass with this change.

```
cd packages/tailwindcss
pnpm vitest run src/canonicalize-candidates.test.ts
```
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Canonicalization: keep `&` when moving a pseudo-element into `*` or `**`" (#20550)

Issues.Title: Canonicalization: avoid exponential collapse when a utility sets many properties
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Fixes #20557.

`canonicalizeCandidates(…, { collapse: true })` took time that doubled with every class in a group of linked candidates.

`collapseGroup` links two candidates when their `otherUtilities` sets (possible replacements) share an entry, and then tries every combination (2^n − n − 1) of each linked group, computing a signature for each. A static utility that sets many properties ends up in the `otherUtilities` of every candidate that sets one of those properties. For example `sr-only` and `not-sr-only` link `relative`, `mt-1`, `w-64`, `overflow-x-auto`, `whitespace-nowrap`, … and a project `@utility` used as a component class does the same, even when the class list doesn't use it.

But such a replacement can never be picked. Its signature can only equal the signature of a combination if every property it sets is also set by a candidate in that combination, and each of those candidates has the replacement in its own `otherUtilities`. `sr-only` also sets `clip-path` and `border-width`, which none of those candidates set, so no combination can ever match it.

This PR changes two things:

1. Before linking, drop every replacement whose properties aren't covered by the candidates that list it. This only uses the property lookups that are already computed, and it only removes replacements that can't match, so the replacements that do get used stay the same. With the impossible ones gone, the giant linked groups split up into the small groups you'd expect (e.g. `overflow-x-*` + `overflow-y-*` → `overflow-*`), so the number of combinations stays small.
2. In the combination loop, skip the (expensive) signature computation for a combination when the intersection of its possible replacements is empty.

Results with the reproduction from the issue (Node 20, same design system per row; times are for one `canonicalizeCandidates` call):

| Case | Classes | Before | After |
| --- | --: | --: | --: |
| A: default theme | 10 | 102 ms | 19 ms |
| | 12 | 369 ms | 22 ms |
| | 14 | 1,374 ms | 20 ms |
| B: default theme + `pill` `@utility` | 12 | 348 ms | 19 ms |
| | 14 | 1,709 ms | 24 ms |
| | 15 | 3,487 ms | 29 ms |
| | 16 | 7,278 ms | 26 ms |

The output was the same before and after for every row, including `text-sm leading-5` → `text-sm/5`, which the issue mentions breaking when the lookup was restricted to matching values instead.

One limit: if a class list really does cover every property of a big utility, its candidates are still linked through it, and that group is still enumerated as before. That's the existing behaviour, and it's much rarer than the cases above.

## Test plan

- Added a regression test with 23 classes linked through `sr-only`, `not-sr-only` and a `pill` `@utility`. It checks the collapsed output (`text-sm leading-5` → `text-sm/5`, everything else untouched) and that it finishes in under 5 s. It takes ~0.8 s on this branch. Without the fix I stopped it after more than 3 minutes.
- `pnpm vitest run packages/tailwindcss/src`: 43 files, 5017 tests passing (this includes all 1805 existing canonicalization tests, whose outputs are unchanged).
- `prettier --check` on the changed files; `tsc` reports no errors for the changed files.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Canonicalization: avoid exponential collapse when a utility sets many properties" (#20558)

Issues.Title: Release loader callbacks after compilation
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Cached compilers retain the module and stylesheet loader callbacks after compilation. Callbacks supplied by build tools can capture completed build state, keeping it alive during later builds.

Capture the `from` and `polyfills` values used by subsequent builds and isolate config and plugin loading from the compatibility theme resolver's scope. This allows the loader callbacks and their captured state to be collected after compilation.

## Test plan

The regression keeps the compiler alive across garbage collection, verifies that both loader callbacks can be collected, and confirms that a subsequent utility build still works.

- `corepack pnpm test:integrations postcss/compiler-lifetime.test.ts` (Node.js 24.19.0)
- `corepack pnpm run test` (Node.js 24.19.0)
- `corepack pnpm build` (Node.js 22.23.3)

The complete integration suite remains unverified locally because several framework fixtures require filesystem and network capabilities unavailable in the sandbox. Lint stopped on generated files and embedded templates; the scoped type check reports the same diagnostics on the unchanged base.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Release loader callbacks after compilation" (#20531)

Issues.Title: Underline the correct occurrence of an unsupported type in `--value(…)`
Issues.Body: ## Summary When an unsupported bare value data type is repeated in `--value(…)`, every warning underlines the first occurrence: ```css @utility paint-* { paint: --value(color, [color], color); } ``` Before, both warnings pointed at the first `color`: ``` --value(color,[color],color) ^^^^^ ``` This happened because the offset was found by replacing every word matching the type with a sentinel in a cloned node and then calling `indexOf` on the printed result, which always returns the first match. Now the offset is computed from the node's position instead: thame, plus the `(`, plus the printed length of the arguments before it. Each warning points at its own occurrence: ``` --value(color,[color],color) ^^^^^ --value(color,[color],color) ^^^^^ ``` ## Test plan Added a test in `packages/tailwindcss/src/utilities.test.ts`. It spies on `console.warn` and checks that the two warnings underline the first and the last color respectively. ``` cd packages/tailwindcss pnpm vitest run src/utilities.test.ts -t "repeated unsupported data type" ``` ## Evidences https://stackblitz.com/edit/github-yq34h5eo?file=input.css before fix: after fix:
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Underline the correct occurrence of an unsupported type in `--value(…)`" (#20554)

Issues.Title: Underline the correct occurrence of an unsupported type in --value
Issues.Body: ## Summary When a `@utility` uses an unsupported bare value data type in `--value(…)`, Tailwind warns and prints the expression with a `^^^` underline under the bad type. If the same type appears more than once, every warning underlines the *first* occurrence: ```css @utility paint-* { paint: --value(color, [color], color); } ``` Before, both warnings pointed at the first color: ``` --value(color, [color], color) ^^^^^ ``` This happened because the underline position came from cloning the function node and replacing every word whose value matched the type with a placeholder. The code then used `indexOf` on that placeholder, which always finds the first match. Now the placeholder only goes into the node being reported. That node's value is swapped for the placeholder, the expression is printed to find the offset, and then the original value is put back. Each warning now points at its own occurrence: ``` --value(color, [color], color) ^^^^^ --value(color, [color], color) ^^^^^ ``` ## Test plan Added a test in `packages/tailwindcss/src/utilities.test.ts`. It spies on `console.warn` and checks that the two warnings underline the first and the last color respectively. ``` cd packages/tailwindcss pnpm vitest run src/utilities.test.ts -t "repeated unsupported data type" ``` ## Evidences https://stackblitz.com/edit/github-yq34h5eo?file=input.css
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Underline the correct occurrence of an unsupported type in --value" (#20553)

Issues.Title: Don't let unbalanced brackets in Pug text leak into the next line
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Fixes #20545

The Pug pre-processor keeps one bracket stack for the whole file. A text or comment line with an unbalanced bracket, like `| (`, pushes a `(` that is never popped, and from then on dots are no longer turned into spaces. So `span.underline.font-bold` on the next line stays one invalid candidate and those classes never get CSS.

This resets the bracket stack at the end of a line, unless we're inside a Pug attribute list (a `(` directly after a tag, class, id or mixin name), since those can span multiple lines. Inside an attribute list the behavior is the same as before.

## Test plan

Added unit tests in `pug.rs` for the cases from the issue (piped text, a `//-` comment, inline text after a tag) plus a multi-line attribute list to make sure that still works. The new test fails without the change.

```
cargo test -p tailwindcss-oxide
```

All 122 unit tests and 71 scanner tests pass.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Don't let unbalanced brackets in Pug text leak into the next line" (#20547)

Issues.Title: Pug: classes not extracted after a text line with an unbalanced `(`
Issues.Body:
### What version of Tailwind CSS are you using?

v4.3.3 (`@tailwindcss/oxide` 4.3.3)

### What build tool (or framework if it abstracts the build tool) are you using?

Vite 8 with `@tailwindcss/vite`, Vue 3 SFCs with `<template lang="pug">`; reproduced with the bare Oxide `Scanner` too.

### Reproduction

`broken.pug`:

```pug
p
  | (
  span.underline.font-bold(title="x") km
  | )
```

`working.pug` (same, but the text lines contain no bracket):

```pug
p
  | x
  span.underline.font-bold(title="x") km
  | x
```

```js
const {Scanner} = require('@tailwindcss/oxide')
for (const f of ['broken.pug', 'working.pug'])
  console.log(f, new Scanner({sources: [{base: __dirname, pattern: f, negated: false}]}).scan()
    .filter(c => ['underline', 'font-bold'].includes(c)))
```

```
broken.pug   []
working.pug  [ 'font-bold', 'underline' ]
```

### Describe your issue

A Pug text line containing an unbalanced opening bracket (here `| (`, which renders a literal "(") stops the
class shorthand on the next tag from being extracted, so those utilities silently get no CSS. Pug itself
renders the template correctly. A real-world case is wrapping a button in parentheses: `| (`, then
`v-btn.px-0.normal-case(...)`, then `| )`.

The cause appears to be the bracket tracking in `crates/oxide/src/extractor/pre_processors/pug.rs`: the
`BracketStack` is kept across the whole file, so the `(` in the text line is pushed and never matched.
While the stack is non-empty, `.` is no longer replaced with a space, so `span.underline.font-bold` stays a
single, invalid candidate. The tag's own attribute parens don't help: its `)` pops only its own `(`.

The same happens inside Vue SFCs (`<template lang="pug">`), where only some of the classes are extracted.

A comment line behaves the same way: `//- a bare "(" here` before the tag reproduces it too.

**Workaround:** write the bracket as an HTML entity (`| (`) or keep brackets balanced on the text line.

**Possible fix:** reset the bracket stack at line boundaries unless the line is inside an attribute list
(Pug attribute lists may span lines, so a plain per-line reset is not enough), or skip piped text (`| ...`)
and comment (`//`, `//-`) lines in the pre-processor.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Pug: classes not extracted after a text line with an unbalanced `(`" (#20545)

Issues.Title: v3: Drop the `braces` dependency chain (`fast-glob`, `micromatch`, `chokidar` v3)
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Tailwind CSS v3 depends on `braces` through three packages: `fast-glob` and `micromatch` (content scanning) and `chokidar` v3 (the CLI's watch mode). `braces` has a published advisory, [GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm) (CVE-2026-93687), that flags every published version. Its maintainer disputes the advisory (see [micromatch/braces#70](https://github.com/micromatch/braces/issues/70)), and this PR takes no position on that: Tailwind's content globs are developer-controlled, so nothing here is exploitable in practice. The practical problem is that there is no `braces` version an install can move to that changes the audit result, so every v3 install currently reports a high-severity finding that fails `npm audit` gates, with no remediation path short of migrating to v4.

This PR replaces the three packages with equivalents that don't depend on `braces`:

| Before | After | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fast-glob` | `tinyglobby` | resolving content globs (`sync`, `escapePath`) |
| `micromatch` | `picomatch` | matching files against content globs |
| `chokidar` v3 | `chokidar` v4 | the CLI's `--watch` mode |

After this change `npm ls braces micromatch fast-glob --omit=dev` is empty.

## Changes

- **`src/lib/content.js`** – `fast-glob`'s `generateTasks` was only used to split the content list into positive and negated patterns, so that is done inline now (same `!(` extglob rule as `fast-glob`). `escapePath` and `sync` map directly onto `tinyglobby` (`expandDirectories: false` keeps `fast-glob`'s behaviour for bare directory entries). `micromatch.matcher` is a thin alias of `picomatch`.
- **`src/cli/build/plugin.js`** – same `sync` → `globSync` swap for the CLI's initial scan.
- **`src/cli/build/watching.js`** – chokidar v4 dropped glob support, so the watcher now watches the base directory of each content path and does the glob matching itself. The filtering mirrors what chokidar v3 did internally for globs: dotfiles match, negated globs act as ignore patterns, and directories that can't contain a matching file are pruned (so `content: ['./*.html']` still doesn't walk `node_modules`). Explicit dependencies (the input CSS, config files, PostCSS dependencies) are tracked separately so they are never filtered out. The two `micromatch.some` call sites keep their exact semantics.
- **`package.json` / `.npmrc`** – `@swc/cli` 0.1.x declares an optional peer dependency on chokidar v3 (only used by `swc --watch`), which npm 7+ treats as a conflict with the root's chokidar v4. The `@swc/cli` releases that accept v4 require Node.js 16+, while v3 still supports Node.js 14, so the repo opts into `legacy-peer-deps` instead. (Side effect in the lockfile: `yaml`, an optional peer of `postcss-load-config`, is no longer auto-installed; nothing in the repo uses it.)
- **`integrations/package.json`** – the integration harness (`integrations/io.js`) used the root's hoisted chokidar implicitly; it now declares its own chokidar v3, because the harness runs on Jest 26 which can't load v4's `node:` imports.

## Verification

- `npm test`: 86 suites / 1062 tests pass on Node 20 and Node 14.
- `npm run build` works on Node 20 and Node 14.
- Integration suites `tailwindcss-cli` (47 tests, including all watcher tests), `content-resolution` (11) and `postcss-cli` (5) pass.
- `npm run style` passes for the changed files.
- `npm ci` from the committed lockfile succeeds.
- A targeted watch-mode check (`content: ['./*.html', './src/**/*.{html,js}', '!./src/ignored/**']`) confirms: `node_modules` and non-matching directories are not traversed, the ignored directory produces no rebuilds, new files in nested and newly created directories trigger rebuilds, files with non-matching extensions don't, and changes to the config file, its dependencies and the input CSS still trigger rebuilds.

## Notes for review

- Behaviour differences I'm aware of: content patterns are no longer brace-expanded before being parsed into base + glob, so `content.files` entries like `./src/**/*.{html,js}` produce one content path instead of two. `tinyglobby` and `picomatch` both handle braces natively, so the resolved files are the same.
- `tinyglobby` is used by Vite, Vitest, Rollup plugins, Storybook and others, and `picomatch` is what `micromatch` wraps, so the matching semantics are shared.
- I ran the same watch-mode check against the unmodified v3 build to compare. One pre-existing quirk shows up in both: when the content list contains a negated glob, the `raw` rename handler's `micromatch.some` check (now `matchesAny`) matches every path, because `!pattern` matches everything *except* `pattern`. So creating e.g. `src/pages/x.css` triggers a rebuild on v3 today. I kept those semantics unchanged rather than silently fix them here; happy to follow up separately if you'd like that fixed.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "v3: Drop the `braces` dependency chain (`fast-glob`, `micromatch`, `chokidar` v3)" (#20541)

Issues.Title: Prefer an existing candidate when collapsing utilities
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Fixes #20539

When collapsing `text-foreground text-primary`, canonicalization returned `text-card-checked-border` if that token had the same default value as `--color-primary`. Signatures are computed from the default theme, so both utilities look identical, but `.dark` can override `--color-primary` and not the other one, so the replacement changes the dark mode color.

`collapseGroup` took the first utility from `potentialReplacements` whose signature matched the combined signature of the combo. It now tries the candidates of the combo itself first. If one of them already produces the same result as the whole combo (here `text-primary`, the one that wins the cascade), it's kept and the others are dropped. Other utilities are only used when none of the originals match, so existing collapses like `h-4 w-4` → `size-4` are unchanged.

## Test plan

- Added a regression test in `canonicalize-candidates.test.ts` with the theme from the issue. It fails on `main` (`text-card-checked-border`) and passes with the change (`text-primary`).
- `pnpm vitest run src/canonicalize-candidates.test.ts` in `packages/tailwindcss`: 1806 passed.
- Whole `packages/tailwindcss` suite: 5015 passed, 1 failed (`variants.test.ts > variants with the same root are sorted deterministically`), which fails the same way on `main` on my machine.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Prefer an existing candidate when collapsing utilities" (#20540)

Issues.Title: fix(upgrade): don't migrate `variant` prop values in expressions or comments
Issues.Body:
Fixes #20435.

The `is-safe-migration` guard for shadcn/ui `variant` props only looked at the text right before the candidate, so any conditional between the prop and the string defeated it. `variant={isActive ? "outline" : "ghost"}` had `outline` rewritten to `outline-solid`, breaking typed variant props loudly and untyped ones silently.

The guard now scans the prop value as an expression: strings inside ternaries, `??`, and comparisons are left alone, while a sibling prop after the variant value (e.g. `className="outline"`) still migrates. Candidates inside `//` and `/* */` comments are skipped too; comment prose is not a class name.

Verified: added 11 cases to `is-safe-migration.test.ts`. 9 fail on pristine code, all 79 pass with the fix. Prettier clean.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(upgrade): don't migrate `variant` prop values in expressions or comments" (#20535)

Issues.Title: Ensure `sr-only` hides the caption of a table
Issues.Body:
Fixes #20510 `sr-only` doesn't hide a `` when it is applied to a `` in Firefox: ```html
…
Visible in Firefox
``` ## Summary `sr-only` hides an element by shrinking it to `1px` and clipping it with `clip-path: inset(50%)`, but neither of those hides a `` in Firefox: - A table can't shrink below the size of its own content, so `width`/`height: 1px` plus `overflow: hidden` clip nothing. - Firefox applies a ``'s `clip-path` to the **inner grid box** of the table, while Chrome and Safari apply it to the **outer table wrapper box** (see [css-tables-3 §3.6.1](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-tables-3/#table-wrapper-box)). A `
` is rendered in the outer table wrapper box, so in Firefox it lives outside the region that `clip-path` clips and stays visible. This is the long-standing [Mozilla bug 1998269](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1998269). Chrome and Safari are unaffected because the box they clip is the one the caption is in. This change clips the caption itself as well, so `sr-only` hides it no matter which box an engine decides to clip: ```css .sr-only > caption { clip-path: inset(50%); } ``` `clip-path` clips painting *and* hit-testing, and it doesn't remove the element from the accessibility tree, which matches how `sr-only` is meant to work. The child selector is deliberately not wrapped in `:where(...)` so that a preflight or user reset can't silently defeat it. `not-sr-only` has to undo the same rule, so the caption becomes visible again for `sr-only md:not-sr-only`: ```css .not-sr-only > caption { clip-path: none; } ``` ## Test plan Two tests were added, both of which fail before this change: 1. `packages/tailwindcss/src/utilities.test.ts` — the `sr-only` snapshot now includes `.sr-only > caption { clip-path: inset(50%) }`. 2. `packages/tailwindcss/tests/ui.spec.ts` — a new test renders a table with a caption and asserts the caption's computed `clip-path` is `inset(50%)`, and a second one checks that `sr-only md:not-sr-only` clips the caption below `md` and unclips both the table and its caption above it. Commands run locally: ```sh # before the change (negative control) $ playwright test --project=chromium --project=webkit -g "sr-only" Expected: "inset(50%)" Received: "none" 2 failed # after the change $ vitest run packages/tailwindcss/src Test Files 42 passed (42) Tests 5015 passed | 1 skipped (5016) $ playwright test --project=chromium --project=webkit 202 passed, 2 skipped ``` I also measured the mechanism directly in Chromium: before the change the caption's computed `clip-path` is `none` and the caption is still hit-testable (`document.elementFromPoint()` over it returns the caption), while the `` itself reports `inset(50%)` and is no longer hit-testable. After the change the caption reports `inset(50%)` and is no longer hit-testable, so it is genuinely hidden and no longer intercepts clicks. One caveat about the test plan: I was not able to run `--project=firefox` in my environment — the headless Firefox bundle Playwright downloads won't launch on this machine (`sandbox_extension_issue_file_to_process failed for …/plugin-container.app: 1 (Operation not permitted)`, and `browserType.launch` then times out), and no system Firefox is installed. So Firefox itself is the one engine I did not observe; the behaviour above comes from the issue report and the spec. The new test asserts the cascade rule rather than an engine-specific box layout, which is why I'd expect it to hold in Firefox too — it should be confirmed by CI.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Ensure `sr-only` hides the caption of a table" (#20528)

Issues.Title: Fix unmet dependency errors by stripping bundledDependencies in WASM package
Issues.Body:
## Problem

When installing `@tailwindcss/postcss` in an environment using strict `npm` (especially `npm 11+`), users experience `ELSPROBLEMS` and `unmet dependency` errors related to the WASM fallback runtime packages (`@emnapi/core`, `@emnapi/wasi-threads`, `@napi-rs/wasm-runtime`, `@tybys/wasm-util`).

The issue stems from `@tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi` listing these packages in both `dependencies` and `bundledDependencies`. Because of how `pnpm` workspaces (which this monorepo uses) handle symlinking, the actual `node_modules` are not fully packed into the published tarball for `bundledDependencies`. When end-users install the package using `npm`, `npm` expects bundled dependencies to already exist inside the downloaded tarball and skips fetching them from the registry. Since they are missing from the tarball, `npm ls` surfaces unmet dependency errors and blocks strict installations.

## Solution

This PR strips the `bundledDependencies` array from `@tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi/package.json`. 

Since these packages are already correctly listed under standard `dependencies`, removing them from `bundledDependencies` forces `npm`, `yarn`, and `pnpm` to correctly fetch and resolve them from the registry during installation, completely eliminating the `npm ls` errors.

**Implementation details:**
1. Manually removed `bundledDependencies` from `crates/node/npm/wasm32-wasi/package.json`.
2. Updated `crates/node/scripts/move-artifacts.mjs` to automatically strip `bundledDependencies` from the package.json during the `postbuild:wasm` lifecycle. This ensures that even if `@napi-rs/cli` automatically injects `bundledDependencies` during `napi build --target wasm32-wasip1-threads`, they are stripped immediately before packing/publishing.

## Verification

Locally verified that the `package.json` in `npm/wasm32-wasi` is correctly mutated post-build and no longer includes `bundledDependencies`, while preserving all functional `dependencies`.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Fix unmet dependency errors by stripping bundledDependencies in WASM package " (#20526)

Issues.Title: Fix Vite input dependency rebuild race
Issues.Body:
## Summary

`Root.generate()` started recording the input stylesheet's modification time without awaiting it. When that `stat` was slower than compilation, the first transform returned with no input entry in `buildDependencies`; a subsequent transform could reuse the old compiler after the stylesheet changed.

Await that dependency record before compiling. The integration test holds just this `stat` pending until it checks the first response, then edits the root stylesheet and checks that the Vite dev server serves the new theme value. The held-stat test failed before the fix and passes afterward.

## Test plan

- `pnpm build` — passed.
- `pnpm test:integrations run vite/input-dependency-race.test.ts` — failed before the fix (first response returned while the input `stat` was pending), passed after.
- `pnpm test:integrations run vite/input-dependency-race.test.ts vite/config.test.ts -t 'rebuilds when the input stylesheet changes before its dependency stat finishes|Config files \(CJS, dev mode\)'` — 2 passed.
- `pnpm exec prettier --check integrations/vite/input-dependency-race.test.ts packages/@tailwindcss-vite/src/index.ts` — passed.

`pnpm lint` did not complete locally: its repository-wide Prettier pass inspected generated WASM build files, and a separate package TypeScript pass reported errors outside the changed files.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Fix Vite input dependency rebuild race" (#20525)

Issues.Title: Respect git global ignore files (core.excludesFile) in source scanner
Issues.Body:
When scanning for source candidates, Oxide previously disabled git global ignore files via `builder.git_global(false)`.

As noted in #15941, the intention was to prevent `.gitignore` files in parent directories outside of a git repository from taking effect, while keeping global ignore files configured in git working. However, calling `git_global(false)` on the walker had the unintended side effect of ignoring `core.excludesFile` (and `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/ignore`) entirely.

This change enables `builder.git_global(true)` so that ignore patterns configured in Git's global configuration are respected during source scanning.

Fixes #20509

## Test plan

- Added unit test `respects_git_core_excludes_file` in `crates/oxide/tests/scanner.rs` verifying that files matched by Git's `core.excludesFile` are skipped.
- Verified that all existing unit and scanner tests continue to pass.

[ci-all]
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Respect git global ignore files (core.excludesFile) in source scanner" (#20524)

Issues.Title: Don't crash when `container` padding uses a screen that isn't a breakpoint
Issues.Body:
## Summary

`buildCustomContainerUtilityRules` (used for the legacy `theme.container` config and by `@tailwindcss/upgrade`) resolves every `padding` key with `theme.resolveValue(key, ['--breakpoint'])` and sorts the result with `compareBreakpoints`. A key that isn't a breakpoint resolves to `null`, and `compareBreakpoints` then calls `null.indexOf('(')`, so the build throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'indexOf')`. The `.filter(Boolean)` after the `map` looks like it was meant to drop those keys, but it runs on the `[key, breakpoint, value]` tuples, which are always truthy.

This happens with a valid v3 config where a padding key is only defined as a `container` screen:

```js
container: {
  padding: { xs: '1rem', md: '2rem' },
  screens: { xs: '30rem', md: '48rem' },
}
```

Without custom `screens`, a padding key that isn't a breakpoint crashes the same way, or, when it is the only one, makes the whole `container` utility disappear because `theme(--breakpoint-xs)` can't be resolved.

The fix filters on the resolved value instead: keys that are neither a breakpoint nor a custom `container` screen are skipped, like in v3. With custom `container` screens, each padding value is added to that screen's own rule, so the sort is only done when there are no custom screens.

## Test plan

- Extended two tests in `packages/tailwindcss/src/compat/container-config.test.ts`. Both fail before the change with the `TypeError` above and pass after it:
  - `padding applies to custom container screens` now has an `xs` container screen with `xs` padding, and the snapshot gains the `@media (min-width: 30rem)` rule with `padding-inline: 1rem`.
  - `allows padding to be defined at custom breakpoints` now has an `xs` padding key that isn't a breakpoint. The snapshot is unchanged because the key is ignored.
- `vitest run src/compat/container-config.test.ts` (in `packages/tailwindcss`)
- `vitest run` (in `packages/tailwindcss`): 42 files, 5015 tests passed
- `prettier --check` on the changed files
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Don't crash when `container` padding uses a screen that isn't a breakpoint" (#20523)
